record.paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
record.context_brief: improving the approximation ratio for 1s-max smti
record.original_question: For the one-sided-ties restriction 1s-max smti, can the current best approximation upper bound be improved all the way down to 5/4?

evidence.quote: It is thus an open problem as to whether this latter upper bound can be reduced to 5/4 in the case of 1s-max smti.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following maximum cardinality stable matching problem, denoted 1s-max-smti. An instance consists of two disjoint finite sets $U$ (men) and $W$ (women). Each man $u\in U$ has a strict preference list over a subset of $W$, while each woman $w\in W$ has a preference list, possibly containing ties (groups of mutually indifferent men), over a subset of $U$. Acceptability is symmetric: $u$ appears on $w$'s list iff $w$ appears on $u$'s list. A matching $M$ is a set of disjoint man–woman pairs $(u,w)$ such that $w$ is on $u$'s list. A pair $(u,w)\notin M$ is called blocking for $M$ if $u$ and $w$ find each other acceptable and each of $u,w$ either is unmatched in $M$ or strictly prefers the other to their current $M$-partner (with ties broken in favor of the current partner). A matching is weakly stable if it admits no blocking pair. The goal is to compute a weakly stable matching of maximum cardinality.

For a constant $c\ge 1$, a polynomial-time algorithm is a $c$-approximation if for every instance it returns a weakly stable matching whose cardinality is at least $1/c$ times the maximum cardinality of any weakly stable matching of that instance.

Problem: Does there exist a polynomial-time $5/4$-approximation algorithm for 1s-max-smti?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to still be open. Under the Unique Games Conjecture, 5/4 is known to be a lower bound on the approximability of 1s-max-smti. The best known approximation ratio for the general (unbounded tie-length) one-sided ties case is 13/9 by Bauckholt, Pashkovich and Sanità (2018), improving on prior bounds (25/17 by Huang–Kavitha, etc.). A matching 5/4 upper bound has been established only in restricted settings (e.g., ties of bounded length, in particular length 2, by Lam and Plaxton), but not for general 1s-max-smti. No paper claiming a 5/4 polynomial-time approximation for the general problem was found.

status_evidence.title: On the approximability of the stable marriage problem with one-sided ties
status_evidence.snippet: Refined analysis giving a 13/9-approximation for stable marriage with one-sided ties.
status_evidence.claim: Best known approximation ratio for general 1s-max-smti is 13/9, still above 5/4.

status_evidence.title: Maximum Stable Matching with One-Sided Ties of Bounded Length
status_evidence.snippet: Approximation ratio 1+(1-1/L)^L for tie length at most L; gives 5/4 for L=2 matching the UG-hardness lower bound.
status_evidence.claim: A tight 5/4 approximation is known only for bounded tie length, not for general one-sided ties.

status_evidence.title: A 25/17-Approximation Algorithm for the Stable Marriage Problem with One-Sided Ties
status_evidence.snippet: Earlier improved upper bound of 25/17 for one-sided ties variant.
status_evidence.claim: Successive improvements have not reached 5/4 for the general problem.
